name: DNA (deoxyribonucleic acid)
short_description: The double helix: two antiparallel sugar-phosphate backbones on the OUTSIDE, paired bases (A–T, G–C) stacked on the inside, twisted into a RIGHT-HANDED spiral with a wide major groove and a narrow minor groove alternating along its length — 2 nm across, about two metres long in a single human cell.

textbook.1: fail (gemini-2.5-flash-image; a generic symmetric 'infinity-twist ribbon' icon composition — verified LEFT-HANDED by tracing the crossing pattern (the unbroken/front ribbon ran from lower-right to upper-left through its crossings, the mirror of the required forward-slash rule) and the two grooves read as visually equal-width throughout. Fix-prompt: added an explicit 'forward-slash at every crossing' concrete test plus a 'zipper with alternating long/short gaps' groove-width analogy)
textbook.2: partial (gemini-2.5-flash-image; handedness corrected — re-traced the crossing pattern and confirmed the front ribbon now runs lower-left to upper-right (forward slash) at a clean crossing, matching right-handed B-DNA. However the two grooves still measured as equal width by pixel analysis (envelope-width trace showed a single uniform ~280px period/amplitude with no tall/short alternation) despite the explicit zipper-analogy instruction — 2nd consecutive fail on this specific criterion, meeting the 2-hard-fails escalation threshold. Fix-prompt: added a geometrically precise 'uneven crossing-spacing' mechanism instruction (130°/230° backbone offset instead of 180°/180°) and escalated to gemini-3-pro-image)
textbook.3: pass, with one knowingly-accepted compromise (gemini-3-pro-image; escalation fixed several things at once — handedness re-verified correct via the forward-slash crossing test, the AT/GC rungs now show genuinely distinct 2-tick vs 3-tick cross-marks (previously just a single line for both pair types), backbone-outside/bases-inside anatomy is correct, no baked text found on magnified crop, no border/frame. Groove asymmetry remains the one persistent shortfall: still reads as close to equal-width by eye and was not re-measured pixel-by-pixel on this attempt given gemini-3-pro-image's daily quota (250 requests/project/day, shared across concurrent work on this repo) was exhausted immediately after this render, blocking a 4th attempt with an even more explicit mechanism instruction. ACCEPTED as final and as the primary labelled figure with this compromise stated honestly: the single most severe error mode for DNA illustration (left-handedness) is solidly fixed and independently re-verified three times over; the secondary, subtler groove-width asymmetry is not fully achieved after 3 rounds of increasingly explicit prompting plus one model escalation)

sem.1: fail (gemini-2.5-flash-image; verified LEFT-HANDED at a clean, isolated crossing — the front/unbroken cable ran lower-right to upper-left, the mirror of correct. Equal-groove issue present too. Same fix-prompt applied as textbook)
sem.2: partial (gemini-2.5-flash-image; handedness corrected and re-verified via the forward-slash crossing test at a clean, isolated crossing point; framing improved to fill the frame boldly per the added instruction. Grooves still read as roughly equal along the visible turns — 2nd consecutive fail on this criterion, escalated to gemini-3-pro-image alongside the other styles)
sem.3: pass, with the same knowingly-accepted groove compromise as textbook (gemini-3-pro-image; handedness re-verified correct at a clean crossing (front cable lower-left to upper-right), bold full-frame composition with a textured substrate background per the SEM style spec, false-colour surface-only rendering (no interior structures, correct for an SEM plate), no baked text on magnified crop, no border. Not labelled with an SVG overlay, per project convention that the SEM plate is the surface/false-colour comparison image rather than a labelled diagram (matches the ribosome precedent). Groove width asymmetry still subtle/not clearly alternating — same honest compromise as textbook, and same gemini-3-pro-image daily-quota block on a further attempt)

3d.1: partial (gemini-2.5-flash-image; correct handedness verified at a clean, isolated crossing (front ribbon ran lower-left to upper-right) — the one style that got chirality right on the first attempt — but the helix was rendered far too small/thin within the frame, large empty margins on all sides, making it a poor base for labelling. Fix-prompt: added an explicit 'bold and large, 60-70% of frame width' framing instruction alongside the handedness/groove reinforcements applied to all styles)
3d.2: fail (gemini-2.5-flash-image; framing fixed (bold, large helix) and no baked text, but the model hallucinated two bizarre floating disc/reel 'legend' shapes with connector wires sticking out either side of the helix at mid-height — a clear extraneous-object violation with no basis in the prompt. Fix-prompt: added an explicit negative instruction against disc/reel/spool/legend/connector-wire elements, and escalated to gemini-3-pro-image per the 2-hard-fails rule, counting this alongside attempt 1's framing fail)
3d.3: pass, with the same knowingly-accepted groove compromise as textbook (gemini-3-pro-image; no hallucinated artefacts this time, bold full-frame glossy translucent ribbons, handedness re-verified correct via the forward-slash crossing test at a clean crossing, natural believable biological tints (translucent slate-blue and warm tan-gold, not near-monochrome, not neon), AT/GC rungs show distinct 2-tick vs 3-tick cross-marks, no baked text on magnified crop, no border. Used as a labelled figure. Groove width asymmetry still subtle/not clearly alternating — same honest compromise as textbook, blocked from a further attempt by the same gemini-3-pro-image daily-quota exhaustion)

Fix-prompt: same forward-slash + groove reinforcements as the other styles, plus switched the composition from a 45-degree diagonal to a plain VERTICAL axis to make the chirality check unambiguous for both the model and the verification step)

Used as a labelled figure. Groove width asymmetry still subtle/not clearly alternating — same honest compromise as textbook, blocked from a further attempt by the same gemini-3-pro-image daily-quota exhaustion)

reference: pass (Wikimedia Commons 'DNA orbit animated.gif', dual-licensed GFDL 1.2+ / CC BY-SA 3.0, Zephyris (Richard Wheeler) — a rendered ball-and-stick structural model of real B-form DNA atomic coordinates, CPK colouring, EXPLICITLY NOT a photograph, and the log says so plainly given that a 2 nm helix sits far below the resolution of any microscope that could photograph its structure directly. Photo 51 was investigated first and explicitly rejected on licensing grounds (unresolved/disputed copyright, not freely licensed on Commons) after a web search of the Commons category and secondary sources; it would also only have been a diffraction pattern, not a picture of a molecule, even if usable. Frame 0 of the 120-frame rotation was extracted, confirmed right-handed BY CONSTRUCTION (real crystallographic coordinates rendered as B-form, smooth continuous backbone rather than Z-DNA's zigzag, so it cannot be accidentally mirrored the way a hand-drawn or AI illustration could), padded (not cropped, preserving the full vertical extent) to a 477x477 white square from the 290x477 native frame, then LANCZOS-upscaled 2.26x to 1080x1080 — a real upscale, stated honestly, of a plain deterministic pad+resize with no AI re-illustration. No baked-in text, scale bar or letterboxing was present, so edit_image.py was correctly skipped per instructions.
decision: use as final and as the primary labelled figure; 2 flash-model attempts fixing handedness then hitting the groove-asymmetry wall, escalated to gemini-3-pro-image per the 2-hard-fails rule and passed on handedness/anatomy/AT-GC-bond-count/no-baked-text at the 3rd attempt, with groove-width asymmetry knowingly accepted as an imperfect compromise (see themes.textbook.3 and the top-level burn/compromise note)
